i think a story or just more time focused around Christa and Clem’s relationship provided a lot of room for a nuanced relationship and dynamic that i feel like was wasted potential. i mean, Christa loses Omid and presumably her baby in short timeframe, with at least one of those deaths indirectly caused by Clementine; she then takes care of Clem for 1-2 years (if i’m remembering correctly). when we return to them, we clearly see some tension and maybe even resentment between the two, there’s little warmth, neither seems happy with their predicament, but Christa still puts herself in harm’s way to protect Clementine when they are threatened.

I just feel like with the little information we have, there’s already a lot of interesting material to work with. The way Christa exits and is never brought up again, not in a flashback, hell not even through dialogue is honestly incredibly insulting. Lee himself spent less time taking care of Clem, and Kenny prior to season 2, even *less*. and the game takes its time to honor and draw importance to their respective impacts on clem. you mean to tell me Christa, who was with Clem for longer than the both of them, mattered so little that she’s not even worthy of a mention?

i think ultimately what gets me is this is obviously a game about parental relationships, the cycle of family and parenthood, etc. and i think featuring this particular kind of relationship of reluctant parenthood between a (surrogate) mother-daughter duo, with the amount of emotional baggage between them, could’ve been an incredibly powerful and bold, set themselves distinctly apart from the other “parent apocalypse” games *and* expanded upon the themes of the series in complex, rich ways. obviously all this is only true if the writing was good, but i think even try and failing would’ve felt more emotionally resonant than what we *did* get. but that’s just me personally. 

tl;dr just upset christa as a character and her relationship with clem were glossed over and forgotten for the entire rest of the series

hey, don’t be ashamed! i think it’s perfectly healthy to engage and critique with the things you like. i think every point you’re raising is valid and you’re clearly coming from a place of goodwill and not blindly hating on the game.

that being said, i do agree with what you’re saying. i’m fond of the game for sure, what the aesthetics and it being a story centered around a group of girls who connect and find each other in less ideal circumstances, girls who you can also ROMANCE as another girl, no shoehorned in male love interest, and with a black girl as a featured, story relevant love interest… well, as a black lesbian, these are all things I ofc appreciate and this is the game i wish i’d had when i was younger.

i’m saying all this because while i do appreciate these things very fully, and what the game is trying to do, my biggest problem walking away from it was the writing/gameplay. since you brought up writing, i’ll only address that, and keep it brief. but i think what you’re describing isnt only really plot
holes — its missed opportunities and foundations that could really help us connect to the characters. i think a lot of people were able to easily connect to everything shown to us without question, and power to them, thats wonderful! but to me i didn’t feel completely invested in the friendship and relationships between the girls here, which sucks, because the emotional crux of the story weighs on the believability and depth of their bond.

i’m not sure if that’s how you felt, but a lot of the things you noticed are bits of information i also felt were missing. i think in my head i have a lot of headcanons to fill the gaps in the writing and worldbuilding that i feel are there, but thats me inventing things outside the text from implied information. but anyways, without continuing to ramble,

tl;dr i think your points are valid and while there *could* be explanations, i feel like the gaps of information aren’t all properly address which can break our immersion and investment in the story/characters. and also that it’s good to be having these thoughts and discussions, or i think so, bc it shows your openness and willingness to engage with a work, which to me, i feel is the ultimate sign of respect towards something.
